answer: When k identities under common control equivocate in a correlated way, the protocol aggregates evidence and applies penalties scaling as O(k^2), rather than treating each signer as an isolated failure. Bonded collateral makes the cost enforceable, while asymmetric depreciation prevents recovery from erasing losses. A sybil swarm therefore incurs an exponential multiplier in capital loss upon detection; like a kernel linking willow trees in an orchard, shared control exposes the coordination.
